Later he joined the Third Crusade and participated in the siege of Acre. He worked alongside Richard the Lionheart and other leaders to press the Muslim hold on the coastline. His diplomatic skill helped secure a truce that left Tripoli under Christian rule for several more years.

*Death and Legacy* Raymond III died in 1187 shortly after the fall of Jerusalem. Some sources say he died of wounds sustained during the siege of Tripoli while others claim he succumbed to illness. His son Raymond IV succeeded him but the county faced increasing pressure from Muslim powers. The eventual loss of Tripoli to the Mamluks in 1289 marked the end of the crusader state. Historians view Raymond III as a pragmatic lord who balanced military action with negotiation to preserve his realm amid shifting crusader fortunes.
